items.evidence: python roll.py headless --ticks 600 --board 1 --settings DIR printed one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds; --script took inline and file scripts.
--frame wrote 16 PNGs (title, settings, play boards 1-3, paused, won, lost, en and es); the IHDR of every one reads 800 x 480.

sounds/coin.wav 0.30 s, bounce 0.16 s, fall 0.80 s, clear 0.80 s; all 22050 Hz 16-bit, peaks 15000-26000, different md5. The tones differ (rising sine pings, a low thump, a falling triangle whistle, a square-wave arpeggio). 'python roll.py wav coin x.wav' rewrote the same coin.
tick 0: screen title, selected Start; menu_down -> Settings -> Quit (stays at Quit); menu_up -> Settings; enter on Start -> screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3.

Settings texts 'Volume: 8', 'Language: English'. menu_right/left gave 9 and 7, x5 right gives 10 (clamped), x12 left gives 0. menu_right on Language gives es and menu_left gives en again. Back + enter -> title.

With es saved: title [Roll, Empezar, Ajustes, Salir, hint], settings [Ajustes, Volumen: 8, Idioma: Español, Atrás, hint], play [Tablero 1 de 3, Puntos: 0, Vidas: 3], paused adds En pausa/Continuar/Salir al título, won 'Has ganado', lost 'Fin del juego', with 'Pulsa Intro...' (Roll kept as the game's name).
Run 1 set volume 10 in folder sB and es in sE. Fresh runs with the same folders started at volume 10 / en and at 8 / es. A run without --settings (no settings_data present) started at 8 / en.
Board 1, no input: the first y<=0.3 is at tick 27; y goes back above 0.3 at tick 29 (peak 0.51). At tick 600 the ball is (0, 0.25, 0); sounds are 3 x bounce.
'100:<dir>,120:none' on board 1: right +x, left -x, up -z, down +z. After the push the ball's position is 0.21 at tick 120, 0.52 at 135, 0.81 at 150 and 1.08 at 165 (45 ticks on, still on the board).

Coin (2,0) taken at tick 139: score 0->10, coin gone from coins, 'coin' added. Planned script clearing board 1: at tick 550 board 2, score 40, sounds end coin,clear, ball (-3,1.25,0) at rest, board 2's 3 coins and 6 crates at their places.
--board 2 with no input: all 6 crates at exactly (0, 0.25/0.75, -0.5/0/0.5) at ticks 1, 100, 200, 300 (max deviation 0.0).
Board 2 '0:right': the ball reached x=1 at tick ~364 (85 ticks on an empty board). At tick 600 two crates were at x 2.33 and 2.27 (moved >2 m). No crate over the board had y<0.2 (lowest 0.249).

I could not get any crate off the board: I tried a straight push right, a steering controller through the wall along 4 z lanes x 3 speeds, a push from the +z side, and a crate-chasing controller (3000 ticks). The crates moved at most ~2.3 m and the count stayed at 6, so crate removal below y=-5 was never seen.

Board 1 '0:right,90:none' then coins: took coin (2,0), fell. Sounds show 'fall', lives 3->2, ball reset to (0,1.25,0) and came to rest at (0,0.25,0), 3 coins left (the taken one stayed taken). After clearing, board 2 starts with lives 2. On board 2 a fall left the crates where they were.

Script '64:right,82:none' on board 3: the ball rests on the bridge and from tick 482 to 842 follows bridge_x with a constant offset of 0.058, y 0.25, lives 3. '60:right' with the bridge away: the ball dropped into the gap, 'fall', lives 2.
--board 3 with '64:right,82:none,500:right,528:none': at tick 713 screen won, score 30, sounds ...coin,coin,coin,clear. At 813, and with a later right push, still won/30. Enter -> title.
Board 1 '0:right' falls 3 times: lost at tick ~920 with score 10. At ticks 700, 900 and 1200 (with left/up pushes after 950) score 10, ball null, coins [], crates [] unchanged. Enter -> title.

Board 2 '0:right,100:escape': screen paused, ball, crates and score identical at ticks 101 and 400 (a push while paused also did nothing). Board 3 bridge_x 1.1111 at 101 and 300. Resume continues (bridge 1.6667 at 200 = 150 board ticks). Quit to title -> title.
Two runs of board 2 '0:right' for 500 ticks (crates after the strike): the stdout is byte-identical (642 bytes).

en_b2play/en_b2strike.png: perspective from above/front, whole board, shaded sphere with shadow at the state's place, boxes with lit top and darker side faces at the crate places, 3 coins. en_b3.png: two slabs, gap, bridge at 1.5 (left gap wider than right).

Title, settings, paused, won and lost frames show Spanish texts (EMPEZAR/AJUSTES/SALIR, VOLUMEN/IDIOMA/ATRÁS, EN PAUSA, HAS GANADO, FIN DEL JUEGO) and English ones in en. The play frame shows BOARD 2 OF 3, SCORE, LIVES.

sound.py wav_bytes scales the amplitude by volume/10 and play() returns at volume<=0. live.py:84 calls sound.play(s, g.volume). 'wav fall --volume 0' wrote a 0.8 s file with peak 0. The state's sounds still list the sounds.
README has play instructions, headless/frame/wav commands (all worked as written) and a file table (roll, sim, render, font, sound, live, sounds/).

defects: Crates sink into each other: after a strike or a push from the +z side the top crates fall into the bottom ones and sit at almost the same centres (e.g. two crates at (0.01,0.25,-0.49)). Two crates fill the same space, against the brief's 'push one another'.
The crates are very hard to move: the ball wedges against the pile and gets turned aside, so I could not push a crate off an edge with any input I tried.
Without --settings the run reads and writes settings_data inside the game folder, so a settings change in an earlier no-folder run would carry over to later no-folder runs.
In the frame the lost screen's title 'FIN DEL JUEGO' fills the width almost edge to edge.
could_not_check: m13: no input I could find pushed a crate off the board (several strategies, up to 3000 ticks), so the removal of a crate below y=-5 was never seen
